subject: Urgent: April usage spike — proposed smoothing / credit options
messages:
From: Ishan Mehta <billing@elasticapps.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@elasticapps.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sharp spike in April usage — urgent billing hold request (Account: ElasticApps)

Hi Vivek,

We just received the April invoice and there's a ~1.2M token spike compared to our typical weekly baseline (~45–60k tokens/day). This is an out-of-character jump and will push us well over our committed band. Can you please pause any collection/auto-pay for this invoice while you investigate?

I've attached a small sample of requests from our side that line up with the surge (elasticapps_sample_rows_apr22.csv). We did a release last week (rolling ingestion) but didn't expect this magnitude of consumption. Our PO/contract is ELAS-2026-4435.

What we need from you:
- Immediate provisional hold on charges while you confirm root cause and provide evidence.
- A clear explanation of why these tokens were attributed to our account.
- An estimate of how long the investigation will take and whether you can issue a provisional credit or smoothing while you reclassify any mis-attributed usage.

This is time-sensitive — collections are configured for Apr 25th. Please advise by EOD PDT.

Thanks,
Ishan Mehta
Head of Platform Engineering
ElasticApps

Attachments: elasticapps_sample_rows_apr22.csv (CSV, 12 rows)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ishan Mehta <billing@elasticapps.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in April usage — urgent billing hold request (Account: ElasticApps)

Ishan — thanks for the heads up and the sample. We're pausing automated collection for the Apr invoice while we run an internal trace. Preliminary steps we will take:

1) Pull your token attribution export for April 1–22 (we've kicked a job to generate usage_export_2027-04-01_30.csv).
2) Have infra/ingest run a tenant trace for the time window you flagged (Apr 14–22).
3) Cross-check any reprocessing or bulk jobs that might have applied a default tenant tag.

Can you confirm whether the release you mentioned included any backfill or reprocessing that might have used a different API key? That will speed root-cause mapping.

We expect an initial update within 48–72 hours. If we find mis-attribution we can either issue a one-time credit or re-bill the corrected quantity; we'll include a smoothing proposal to avoid a single-large spike on your Apr invoice.

I'll follow up with an internal note to get engineering eyes on this now.

— Vivek
Director, Sales (Strategic)
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sharp spike in April usage — urgent billing hold request (Account: ElasticApps)

Ben — forwarding ElasticApps' billing note. Vivek has paused collection for now. Can you pull a trace and check for the following:
- Tenant tag churn around Apr 14–22 for account ELAS-2026-4435
- Any backfill/reprocessing jobs launched by internal tools that default to a global tenant id
- Log lines showing request_id -> tenant_id mapping so we can reassign tokens if needed

Attachments they provided are small sample rows. I've asked them to confirm whether they used a different API key during the release. If you find mis-attribution, please produce a short CSV with reattributed token counts by day so I can include it in the customer-facing note.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

> On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 11:35 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ishan — thanks for the heads up and the sample. We're pausing automated collection for the Apr invoice while we run an internal trace.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in April usage — urgent billing hold request (Account: ElasticApps)

Quick update from infra tracing (preliminary):
- We located a reprocessor job kicked on Apr 15 that ingested archived requests and replayed them into the inference pipeline. The job omitted tenant mapping for ~85% of replays and defaulted to the account-scoped anonymous tenant id which maps to ElasticApps' primary billing entity.
- Based on request_id sampling and KV cache hits, approx. 1,052,400 tokens were attributed to ELAS-2026-4435 as a direct consequence of that replay.
- Attached is a short trace snippet showing request_id -> assigned_tenant (trace_snippet_apr22.log).

Suggested remediation path:
1) Re-run attribution for Apr 15–20 with correct tenant mapping and produce a reattribution CSV (day, original_tokens, corrected_tokens).
2) If reattribution confirms the numbers above, ops can reclassify the tokens and billing will adjust retroactively.
3) For short-term customer impact, propose a smoothing option: either (A) issue a provisional credit equal to the reattributed token charge now, or (B) amortize the adjustment across the next 3 invoices to avoid a single-month shock.

I'll produce the reattribution CSV by EOD PST and attach evidence.

— Ben
Sr. Platform Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: trace_snippet_apr22.log (log excerpt)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ishan Mehta <billing@elasticapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in April usage — proposed smoothing / credit options (Account: ElasticApps)

Ishan — thanks for your patience. Short summary and proposed next steps: 

What we found:
- A replay/backfill job launched Apr 15 inadvertently left tenant mapping unset for a large portion of replayed requests. That caused ~1.05M tokens to be attributed to ELAS-2026-4435 instead of their original tenant assignments. Evidence and a trace excerpt are attached.

Options we can offer (please indicate preference):
1) Immediate provisional credit for the reattributed charge (same-day credit to April invoice) and full reattribution in our billing system so the Apr invoice is corrected. We will release the collection hold once the credit posts.
2) Amortize the correction across your next 3 invoices (smoothing) to avoid a material hit in a single month. We'll post a credit memo that reduces future invoices accordingly.

We will also:
- Share the reattribution CSV by EOD PST (Ben is preparing it).
- Add a guard to the reprocessor to prevent default tenant assignment on replays.

Please reply with which option you prefer (Immediate credit vs. smoothing). If neither works, propose an alternative and we'll execute.

If I don't hear back by Mon Apr 26th 17:00 PDT we'll provisionally schedule option 1 (immediate credit) to avoid collections impact.

Best,
Vivek
Director, Sales (Strategic)
Redwood Inference
